question: Should OpenClaw core own the proposed V1 ordered-layer composition, first-declaration authority, monotonic tool-policy tightening, and immutable startup boundary?
rationale: Existing `$include` composition does not preserve independent source authority, so this is a genuine new core capability whose compatibility and security semantics cannot be accepted by automated review alone.

options.title: Accept the narrow V1 seam
options.body: Approve the startup-only opt-in contract after configuration and security owners verify RFC-to-implementation parity and no-flag compatibility.

options.title: Narrow the contract further
options.body: Keep the RFC open while revising authority, tightening, write-blocking, or lifecycle rules that maintainers do not want to freeze.

options.title: Keep layering host-owned
options.body: Decline the core seam and require Lobster and other hosts to continue flattening configuration outside OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow V1 seam
recommendation.body: Approve the startup-only opt-in contract after configuration and security owners verify RFC-to-implementation parity and no-flag compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-cutting core product and security-boundary decision, and the repository plus PR timeline identify this person as the best available decision owner.
